analysis.title: BOJ's hawkish hold: target reached, more rate hikes to come
key_insights: The BOJ held its policy rate at 1.25% on 30 October. The vote was 8-1, with Hajime Takata dissenting in favour of an immediate hike. September's vote was 7-2, with both dissenters voting against a rate hike.
Amova reads the split as modestly more hawkish. September's dovish dissenters appear to have accepted the current rate, while Takata argued for a faster pace of accommodation removal toward neutral.

The BOJ Outlook Report says underlying CPI inflation is at a level generally consistent with the 2% price stability target. It warns that inflation expectations and corporate pricing behaviour could push inflation above target. It reaffirmed that it will keep raising rates in response to the economy and prices.

The BOJ will double the pace of ETF disposals from 2027, to an annual 0.1% of stock market trading value, roughly 860 billion yen on a book value basis. At that pace the disposal would still take 43 years. The BOJ cited buoyant market conditions and said sales may be adjusted or suspended depending on future financial conditions.
The BOJ raised its FY26 growth forecast from 0.6% to 0.7% and lowered FY27 growth from 0.8% to 0.7%. It raised its FY27 core CPI median forecast from 2.4% to 2.6%.
The BOJ names energy costs, yen depreciation and AI-related demand as potential sources of upside inflation pressure. Amova notes that pass-through to consumer prices is not automatic.

The BOJ expects consumption to stay relatively flat over fiscal 2026 before recovering as price pressures ease. Amova says nominal wage gains alone do not restore household confidence, and that contained inflation expectations help keep real wage growth expectations intact.

Amova's expectations for BOJ tightening are modestly below the hikes priced into the OIS market. The September median forecast of its Global Investment Strategy Committee (GISC) was two more BOJ hikes in the next 12 months, taking the policy rate to 1.75% by September 2027.
Dollar/yen moved little after the BOJ decision. Amova says this may indicate the pair remains driven more by US economic expectations and the Fed rate path.

The Fed held rates on 28 October with a 10-2 vote and emphasised upside inflation risks. Amova's analysis shows higher policy-message alignment between the Fed and Chair Kevin Warsh and a rise in inflation emphasis.
Warsh acknowledged a need to refine his understanding of US productivity ahead of the Fed Productivity and Jobs Taskforce on 16 November.

Amova says the global risk-tolerant expansion depends heavily on robust nominal US growth, buoyant earnings expectations and benign financing conditions, which underpin the carry trade. It expects tighter overall financial conditions to reduce the accommodation supporting risk assets over time.

In its Bayesian FOMC model update, Amova finds policy-message alignment and inflation emphasis rose the most, and confidence in less forward guidance was modestly reinforced. Productivity conviction rose but the meaning of 'productivity' remains unclear. Balance sheet and governance views remain weakly identified.

Amova flags an inconsistency: if productivity were durably rising, r-star (the neutral rate) could also be higher, which implies a higher rather than lower neutral rate. Warsh has not publicly addressed this implication.

tension_points.theme: BOJ hike path vs market pricing
tension_points.bull_case: The BOJ confirmed inflation is consistent with its 2% target, raised its FY27 core CPI forecast to 2.6%, doubled ETF disposals and kept a tightening bias. Takata voted for an immediate hike. Amova expects two more hikes to 1.75% by September 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Amova's expected tightening is modestly below what the OIS market prices. Pass-through to consumer prices is not automatic, and consumption is expected to stay flat over fiscal 2026.
